column3: Close to the Greek; “the loaves of the presentation” is rendered “the showbread.”
NKJV has “One greater,” following the Textus Receptus (masculine); the critical text has the neuter, “something greater.” NKJV adds “in this place.”
NKJV includes “even,” following the Textus Receptus.
Close to the Greek; “a smoldering wick” is rendered “smoking flax.”
Close to the Greek; “hope” is rendered “trust.”
NKJV reads “the blind and mute man both spoke and saw,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “so that the mute man spoke and saw.”
NKJV spells the name “Beelzebub,” as in the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Beelzebul.”
NKJV names “Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “knowing … He said.”
